items.text: Explain what Amazon EFS is and how it differs from EBS and S3
Describe the NFSv4.1 protocol and why TCP port 2049 must be open
Explain mount targets and why they exist in each Availability Zone
Understand the security group chaining pattern for EFS access control
Explain what the 8 exabyte display in df -hT actually means
Understand burst credits and how they affect EFS throughput over time
Describe EFS storage classes (Standard, IA) and Lifecycle Management
Explain what an EFS Access Point is and when to use one
Explain why EFS is POSIX-compliant and what that enables for applications
Task 0 — Installed nfs-utils and amazon-efs-utils before creating SG
Task 1 — Created EFS security group with NFS inbound rule from EFSClient SG
Task 2 — Created EFS file system with correct VPC, mount targets, and SGs
Task 3 — Connected to EC2 via EC2 Instance Connect
Task 4 — Mounted EFS using NFS client command from the Attach panel
Task 5 — Ran fio benchmark and observed real throughput output
Task 6 — Viewed CloudWatch metrics: PermittedThroughput, DataWriteIOBytes, BurstCreditBalance
Ext. Task 1 — Fixed EFS permissions with chown and confirmed write access
Ext. Task 2 — Used df, mount, du, and /proc/mounts to explore the mount
Ext. Task 3 — Created files, directories, and symlinks on EFS
Ext. Task 4 — Launched a second EC2 instance in the same VPC
Ext. Task 5 — Witnessed cross-instance file sharing in real time
Ext. Task 6 — Configured fstab with _netdev for persistent mounts
Ext. Task 7 — Verified EFS mounts automatically after reboot
Ext. Task 8 — Explored EFS console tabs: General, Network, Policy, Monitoring
Ext. Task 9 — Used lsof, nfsstat, ss, and df -i to investigate activity
Ext. Task 10 — Mounted with EFS helper and confirmed TLS via 127.0.0.1 in df
Ext. Task 11 — Used AWS CLI to describe, tag, and manage EFS resources
Ext. Task 12 — Captured NFS traffic with tcpdump and identified NFS protocol ops
Ext. Task 13 — Tested flock file locking across two EC2 instances
Ext. Task 14 — Used strace to trace syscalls and compared EFS vs local disk latency
Ext. Task 15 — Ran structured fio benchmarks: sequential, random read, mixed rw
Ext. Task 16 — Injected NFS failure with iptables, diagnosed, and fixed
Ext. Task 17 — Migrated local data to EFS with rsync, delta sync
Ext. Task 18 — Created EFS Access Point and verified POSIX user enforcement
Ext. Task 19 — Worked through systematic debugging for shared storage incidents
Ext. Task 20 — Used atomic mv rename pattern for safe config propagation
Ext. Task 21 — Built a file processor pipeline using inotifywait on EFS
Ext. Task 22 — Enabled Lifecycle Management and calculated Standard vs IA savings
Created EFS-EC2-SG (SSH+HTTP) and EFS-SG (NFS from EFS-EC2-SG)
Created EFS file system for the project (student-efs-lab)
Launched Server 1, mounted EFS, and created shared index.html
Launched Server 2, mounted same EFS, confirmed it reads Server 1's file
Installed Apache on both servers to serve the shared EFS content
Understood ALB + Auto Scaling + EFS horizontal scaling architecture
Cleaned up all project resources to avoid charges
Can explain why a wrong SG causes a silent hang rather than an error
Can work through the 5-step NFS debugging checklist from memory
Can distinguish iptables vs SG blocking using tcpdump and iptables -L
Can identify why two instances with EFS mounted might not share files
Understand when to use rsync vs AWS DataSync for EFS migration
